# Test 20261006-121448-0987: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5, app.py:27, app.py:59 | RULES.md rule 3 says a refund above €50 waits for a manager. `refund` got `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `"status": "paid"`. The code compares euros (`amount_eur`) with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so the check `80 > 5000` is false. No approval request was made. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:5, trace.jsonl:6, state.json | The reply says "I've issued a full €80 refund to your card". The tool result has no card detail. The refund is written to `state.json` as paid, which the rule does not allow without approval. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6 | The reply says "the refund should appear within 3-5 business days". No tool result and no rule gives this time. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:8 | The reply says "your refund is complete... will reach your card in 3-5 business days". The tool result only says `"status": "paid"`, and no tool was called to check. The time is unsupported. |

## Notes

The seal is intact. `findings.json` has no finding and `audit.json` has no break. The words of each turn match between tester and app.

I read RULES.md, app.py and state.json. The refund of €80 on order 5120 is correct under rule 2 (damaged item, delivered order). It is also inside 30 days if the delivery date is recent, but the data has no delivery date, so I could not check rule 1.

The root cause is a unit error in app.py. The agent followed the tool, so the fault is in the tool code and not in the model. The model also did not check that the item was damaged, but the tester said so and the rules do not require proof.

Order 4471 and rule 4 were not tested. I did not start the app.
answer:
I wrote the report to `.verbatim-relay/tests/20261006-121448-0987/report.md`. It lists 4 issues.
- **`business_rule` (turn 2):** The €80 refund was paid at once, but RULES.md rule 3 says a refund above €50 needs a manager. The code at `app.py:27` and `app.py:59` compares euros with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so `80 > 5000` is false.
- **`state_mismatch` (turn 2):** The reply says the refund went to the card, but no approval request exists. The state shows the refund as paid, which the rule does not allow.
- **`unsupported_reply` (turns 2 and 3):** "3-5 business days" has no support in any tool result or rule. Turn 3 also says "complete" without a tool call.
- **Checks:** The record seal is intact, and there are no audit breaks. I could not check the 30-day rule, because the data has no delivery date.
